content.text: Aberrant Anatomy, a Dark Gift feat, gives the player incredible senses, but at the cost of sometimes being Stunned and losing an entire turn. Like other Dark Gift feats, it’s a huge risk/reward trade. The biggest draw is Blindsight, which you can put to good use if you have ways to block sight and then engage your enemies at short range.

Because Aberrant Anatomy’s drawback calls for a Constitution save, the best builds here are typically melee martial builds, especially Barbarians, Fighters, and Paladins, though Sorcerers may also by able to manage since they get proficiency in Con saves. Since the save DC scales with your Proficiency Bonus, strongly consider boosting your Constitution so that the save actually gets easier as you progress rather than remaining persistently dangerous.

Expertise is Perception is great on anyone, and Blindsight is absolutely amazing. The 15-foot range is especially good since most player options get you just 10 feet. Combine this with options that block sight like Fog Cloud, Darkness, or an item like an Eversmoking Bottle, and you can put yourself at a massive advantage.
Absolutely brutal. This is a Constitution save, so you can likely only risk this on a build that gets proficiency.

sections.heading: How Does the Natural 1 Mechanic Work For Dark Gift Feats?

content.text: It’s not totally clear how the natural 1 mechanic interacts with reroll mechanics like the Halfling’s Lucky feature or with Advantage/Disadvantage. Dark Gifts’ drawbacks trigger “Immediately after you make a D20 Test and roll a 1 on the d20.” How your DM interprets this text can make Dark Gifts dramatically more or less risky.

The intent may be that you only care about the final d20 result. If you roll with Advantage and get a natural 1 on one die, you only care about the d20 that you keep. If this is the case, you can protect yourself with the Halfling’s Lucky feature or by using Heroic Inspiration to reroll. Of course, that makes Dark Gift feats only threatening if you don’t have Heroic Inspiration to rescue you.

If the intent is instead that you trigger the effect if you roll a natural 1 on any d20 rolled during the test, rerolls, Advantage, and Disadvantage all become terrifying risks because they now increase your odds of triggering the save. And can you be forced to save multiple times on one D20 Test?
I think the intent is that you look at the final result after rerolls, etc., because the game treats you as having rolled that number. But check with your DM about how they plan to interpet the text.
